title: Compute-Matched Evaluation of Transform-Augmented GRPO for Mathematical Reasoning

The purpose of the contribution is to determine whether TA-GRPO's reported gains over standard GRPO come from its semantic transformation mechanism or merely from 4x more rollouts. No prior paper explicitly investigates this specific empirical relationship between rollout count and semantic transformation mechanism in GRPO-based RL. While several papers (e.g., [2], [4], [5], [9], [17]) discuss rollout efficiency, allocation strategies, or optimization techniques, none establish or report the same empirical relationship between these variables. The mechanism involves a compute-matched evaluation where TA-GRPO and standard GRPO consume identical total rollouts (~725K) to isolate the effect of semantic transformation. Papers such as [4], [5], [9], and [17] discuss rollout allocation strategies or efficiency improvements, but none describe a compute-matched evaluation design specifically isolating semantic transformation effects under identical rollout budgets. This mechanism is **NONE**.  

**Evaluation:**  
The evaluation design compares TA-GRPO and GRPO-Long under identical rollout budgets, measuring Pass@32 performance gains. Papers such as [20] and [6] use Pass@k metrics for reasoning evaluation, and [4], [5], [9], and [17] conduct rollout-based comparisons. These prior works employ similar evaluation designs (e.g., rollout budget comparisons, Pass@k metrics), even if applied to different models or settings. Thus, the evaluation is **COVERED**.  

**Domain:**  
The domain is RL for LLM mathematical reasoning. Papers such as [6], [12], and [14] explicitly address RL for mathematical reasoning in LLMs, making this domain **COVERED**.

### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to decompose TA-GRPO's improvement into its two constituent mechanisms. No prior paper explicitly reports or establishes the same empirical relationship — the decomposition of TA-GRPO's improvement into semantic data augmentation and pooled advantage normalization contributions. While several papers discuss related RL techniques (e.g., [2], [3], [6], [8], [18]), none of them focus on decomposing TA-GRPO's improvement into these specific mechanisms. Therefore, the purpose is **NONE**.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves an ablation condition that uses transformations but computes advantages per-variant rather than pooled, isolating data augmentation from pooled advantage normalization. Paper [5] ("Generalization in Reinforcement Learning by Soft Data Augmentation") introduces SOft Data Augmentation (SODA), which decouples augmentation from policy learning, aligning with the idea of isolating augmentation effects. Paper [10] ("Bootstrap Advantage Estimation for Policy Optimization in Reinforcement Learning") uses data augmentation to compute bootstrap advantage estimation, which is conceptually similar to isolating advantage computation mechanisms. Both papers contain substantively equivalent mechanisms, so the mechanism is **COVERED**.

The evaluation design reports that 87% of TA-GRPO's improvement comes from semantic data augmentation, while only 13% comes from pooled advantage normalization. Papers [5] and [10] both evaluate the impact of data augmentation on RL performance, but neither uses the exact evaluation design of decomposing improvement percentages into constituent mechanisms. No prior paper explicitly uses this decomposition-based evaluation design. Therefore, the evaluation is **NONE**.

### Domain
The domain is RL training mechanism analysis. Papers [2], [3], [5], [6], [8], [10], [18], and others all operate within the RL domain, analyzing training mechanisms, advantage estimation, or data augmentation. This contribution falls squarely within the same general application area. Therefore, the domain is **COVERED**.
